# Description

Concurrent GEMMs on independent CUDA streams receive the same cuBLAS workspace from the device/mode cache and can overwrite each other's partial sums. On one H200, two FP32 `NT` GEMMs with a reduction dimension of 16384 produced incorrect results in 35 of 48 calls; separate scratch produced zero mismatches against serial execution.

Replace the Python workspace cache with invocation-local memory owned by PyTorch's CUDA allocator. Ordinary GEMMs allocate a native `DataPtr` in the PyTorch binding, avoiding per-call Python Tensor creation. The list/multistream grouped path uses one allocation with disjoint, 256-byte-aligned workspace slices. Its helper streams join the caller before the owner is released. Eager reuse remains stream-ordered; captured allocations belong to their graph's private pool. No persistent per-stream cache or new device synchronization is added.

Custom recipes and communication overlap retain explicit Tensor workspaces. Existing explicit-workspace callers remain supported; the private bindings additionally accept `None` with size zero to request native allocation. Usable workspace sizes, GEMM dtypes and algorithm selection are unchanged. The grouped-tensor backend is unchanged.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

- Allocate scratch per invocation in the PyTorch native binding for ordinary and list/multistream grouped GEMMs.
- Remove Linear and BasicLinear's preallocation workaround for globally cached scratch.
- Test eager ownership, temporary-stream cleanup, graph-pool isolation across capture generations, concurrent FP32/BF16 graph replay, grouped GEMM numerics, and compiled opaque-GEMM graph generations. Observe native allocation requests without retaining Tensor references.
- Cover router dgrad NN with `weight[128,4096]`, `grad_output[8192,128]`, output `[8192,4096]`, and reduction 128 against exact analytic references in FP32 and BF16. Preserve NT coverage.
- Include the workspace regression in the PyTorch L0 launcher.

## Validation

Exception-path follow-up (`efa5063`, October 26): the common grouped launch now rejoins helper streams before rethrowing a recoverable GEMM error. On H200, the old core reproduces `cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnjoined`; the rebuilt core and PyTorch binding pass all **23 workspace tests**, including the new partial-group failure/capture/recovery regression. Formatting, cpplint and the license check pass. No host/device-wide synchronization or additional successful-path CUDA calls were added. The earlier performance measurements below were not rerun for this exception-path change.

The following records the earlier native-allocation qualification:

H200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA toolkit 13.0, cuBLASLt 13.5.1, native PyTorch CUDA allocator. The candidate binding was rebuilt with the same flags as main `9ea05cf2e8dc`, using the unchanged common library.

- All 22 cases in `tests/pytorch/test_gemm_workspace.py` pass, including the compiled opaque-GEMM capture-generation case, with no skips.
- Three additional local operational regressions pass. The same independent-stream and concurrent graph-generation fixtures fail on main; both the prior PR revision and native implementation pass. Temporary-stream cleanup and invalid-request checks also pass.
- A two-H200 quantized-wrapper check confirms that device selection follows actual storage and restores the caller's device.
- All 288 paired benchmark comparisons have bitwise-identical outputs and module input/parameter gradients; 18 targeted recheck comparisons also match.
- Six alternating main/candidate process pairs cover three shapes, BF16/block FP8, GEMM/grouped GEMM/Linear/GroupedLinear, and eager/graph execution. Small eager GEMM completion overhead is +1.65% BF16 and +3.48% FP8; grouped GEMM is +0.14%/+0.59%. Small Linear forward/backward is +0.05%/+1.51%, and GroupedLinear is -0.53%/-0.11%. These are paired medians, not universal bounds. CUDA graph replay is measured separately; median changes are within ±1% in these cases. Detailed timing, warmup flags and rechecks are in the benchmark comments below.
- Pre-commit, scoped pylint/cpplint and the L0 license checker pass on macOS. Changes after GPU qualification are repository formatting only.
- Follow-up in `48a48c91896a`: update both Linear compile-test observers to the native binding. Both edited observers pass H200 capture checks through the compiled-GEMM fixture; the full Linear tests remain capability-skipped (11 cases) on the available PyTorch 2.13 build, pending the compatible opaque-object CI environment.
- Full L0 validation of the new native revision remains pending CI. These tests do not establish full-model throughput, distributed-overlap performance or alternate allocator support.

# Checklist

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

I also traced the cuDNN/CuTeDSL paths. In our frontend 1.26 runtime, the compiled operators retain mutable workspace, and the wgrad launch closures capture it. The follow-up should reuse compiled kernels but separate workspace ownership for overlapping calls and graph lifetimes, then measure eager enqueue cost and graph replay separately. # Description

Concurrent GEMMs on independent CUDA streams receive the same cuBLAS workspace from the device/mode cache and can overwrite each other's partial sums. On one H200, two FP32 `NT` GEMMs with a reduction dimension of 16384 produced incorrect results in 35 of 48 calls; separate scratch produced zero mismatches against serial execution.

Replace the Python workspace cache with invocation-local memory owned by PyTorch's CUDA allocator. Ordinary GEMMs allocate a native `DataPtr` in the PyTorch binding, avoiding per-call Python Tensor creation. The list/multistream grouped path uses one allocation with disjoint, 256-byte-aligned workspace slices. Its helper streams join the caller before the owner is released. Eager reuse remains stream-ordered; captured allocations belong to their graph's private pool. No persistent per-stream cache or new device synchronization is added.

Custom recipes and communication overlap retain explicit Tensor workspaces. Existing explicit-workspace callers remain supported; the private bindings additionally accept `None` with size zero to request native allocation. Usable workspace sizes, GEMM dtypes and algorithm selection are unchanged. The grouped-tensor backend is unchanged.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

- Allocate scratch per invocation in the PyTorch native binding for ordinary and list/multistream grouped GEMMs.
- Remove Linear and BasicLinear's preallocation workaround for globally cached scratch.
- Test eager ownership, temporary-stream cleanup, graph-pool isolation across capture generations, concurrent FP32/BF16 graph replay, grouped GEMM numerics, and compiled opaque-GEMM graph generations. Observe native allocation requests without retaining Tensor references.
- Cover router dgrad NN with `weight[128,4096]`, `grad_output[8192,128]`, output `[8192,4096]`, and reduction 128 against exact analytic references in FP32 and BF16. Preserve NT coverage.
- Include the workspace regression in the PyTorch L0 launcher.

## Validation

Exception-path follow-up (`efa5063`, October 26): the common grouped launch now rejoins helper streams before rethrowing a recoverable GEMM error. On H200, the old core reproduces `cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnjoined`; the rebuilt core and PyTorch binding pass all **23 workspace tests**, including the new partial-group failure/capture/recovery regression. Formatting, cpplint and the license check pass. No host/device-wide synchronization or additional successful-path CUDA calls were added. The earlier performance measurements below were not rerun for this exception-path change.
